stories.headline: Nvidia Printed $96.2 Billion and Then Did Something It Had Never Done: Forecast a Whole Year
stories.key_takeaway: Nvidia beat a blowout quarter with an unprecedented year-ahead forecast of 70% growth, but the guidance is capped by supply rather than demand, and it arrives alongside $279 billion in supply commitments and $108.5 billion in customer guarantees that are squeezing margins.

pull_quote.text: We recognize the scale of this support, and we know some will call this circular financing. We see it differently.

stories.article_excerpt: Nvidia has spent three years training Wall Street to expect the impossible and then beating it anyway. On Wednesday it did both again.

stories.headline: Anthropic Just Bought Six Years of Electricity in West Virginia for $45 Billion
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic's reported $45 billion, six-year lease of 460 megawatts at Nscale's West Virginia campus fills the slot Microsoft abandoned and becomes 88% of the two-year-old firm's IPO backlog, binding two pre-IPO companies to each other's execution.

pull_quote.text: The reported $45 billion agreement for computing capacity at Nscale's West Virginia campus is an extraordinary vote of confidence in our state and the strategy we put in place.

stories.article_excerpt: Strip the zeroes off Anthropic's newest compute deal and what is left is a utility bill.

stories.headline: Nvidia Is Buying the Neutral Ground. Hugging Face Goes for $12.9 Billion.
stories.key_takeaway: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to pay $12.9 billion, roughly 86x revenue, for the vendor-neutral hub where every chipmaker's models are published.

pull_quote.text: It is positive for open-model funding and adoption but potentially negative for ecosystem neutrality. The concern is that an important neutral marketplace could gradually become an Nvidia-centered distribution channel.
pull_quote.role: Founder and Chief Research Officer, Tekonyx

stories.article_excerpt: Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, The Information reported Wednesday night.

stories.headline: AWS Ordered Two Million More GPUs. It Also Builds Its Own Chips.
stories.key_takeaway: AWS doubling down on 2 million more Nvidia GPUs while its own Trainium chips adopt Nvidia memory and interconnect shows hyperscalers are not replacing Nvidia with custom silicon, they are running both books.

pull_quote.text: NVIDIA and AWS have built one of the great growth engines of the AI era, and demand is running ahead of every forecast.

stories.article_excerpt: Amazon Web Services will deploy 2 million additional Nvidia GPUs across its global infrastructure in 2027 and 2028.

stories.headline: The AI Bottleneck Moved to Memory. Kioxia and Sandisk Are Spending $31 Billion on It.
stories.key_takeaway: Kioxia and Sandisk's $31 billion Japan plan expands NAND flash capacity through 2032, but NAND is not HBM, so it relieves the AI storage tier rather than the high-bandwidth memory shortage throttling GPU output.

pull_quote.text: We sincerely appreciate the support of the Japanese government to date and recognize the importance of its continued strategic support in maintaining further strengthening our global competitiveness.

stories.article_excerpt: For two years, the story of AI scarcity had a single face: the GPU. On Thursday, Kioxia and Sandisk made another case.

stories.headline: A Consumer AI Assistant Still in Private Beta Just Raised $250 Million
stories.key_takeaway: Instinct's $250M Series B at a $2.5B valuation took roughly three-quarters of the day's disclosed venture capital for a product nobody can sign up for, while the rest went to small vertical-AI rounds.

pull_quote.text: The more powerful these agents become, the more trust matters. Every successful action earns a little more trust. One unauthorized action can reset that trust to zero.

stories.article_excerpt: On Wednesday, a product you almost certainly cannot use raised a quarter of a billion dollars.

stories.headline: Google's New Transcription Model Deletes Your Filler Words. That Is the Point.
stories.key_takeaway: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe's headline 2.6% word error rate is an English-only, eight-hour benchmark measured on verbatim mode, which means the standard metric cannot evaluate the silent-editing feature Google is actually selling.

pull_quote.text: Unlike conventional speech recognition models that struggle with background noise, complex jargon, and disfluency cleanup, Gemini 3.5 Transcribe converts raw audio directly into accurate, polished, formatted text.
pull_quote.role: Senior Director of Engineering, Gemini Audio, Google

stories.article_excerpt: The most consequential line in Google's new transcription launch is not a benchmark number. It is a configuration flag.

stories.headline: Salesforce Spent Twenty Years Building Screens. Now It Is Shipping Its CRM Into Claude.
stories.key_takeaway: Salesforce is betting that its decades of data, metadata and encoded workflows are the real moat and that the interface was always disposable.

pull_quote.text: The value of Salesforce is not in our UI itself. It's not the application. The value of Salesforce is in the data and the metadata, the years worth of encoded workflows and business practices that have been built up inside of Salesforce.
pull_quote.role: President of Applications and Marketing, Salesforce

stories.article_excerpt: Salesforce spent twenty-seven years teaching the business world to click. Now it is handing the front door to a rival.

stories.headline: OpenAI Turned On Ads in India. Three Hundred Thirty Million Users, Rs 725 a Day to Reach Them.
stories.key_takeaway: With ad revenue per Indian user likely under fifty cents a year, advertising is not a bridge to subscriptions in OpenAI's largest market but the permanent business model for 330 million people who will never pay.

pull_quote.text: The sponsored card sits below an answer that the AI has already generated. If the model does not recommend you in its organic response, you are essentially paying for ad space to argue with the AI.

stories.article_excerpt: OpenAI switched on advertising inside ChatGPT in India on Thursday, in its largest market by users.

stories.headline: Two Engineers and an AI Designed a Processor in Two Weeks. Nobody Has Made It Yet.
stories.key_takeaway: Architect Labs' AI generated a verified inference accelerator in under two weeks, but the claim covers only front-end RTL and functional verification on an FPGA. Every physical-design and manufacturing risk remains untested.

pull_quote.text: If independently validated and successfully translated from a programmable prototype into manufactured silicon, the project could represent a major change in how computer chips are developed.

stories.article_excerpt: The claim landed Thursday with the kind of superlative that makes veteran chip engineers reach for the mute button.

stories.headline: A $399 Walking Robot Is Hugging Face's Answer to the Humanoid Arms Race
stories.key_takeaway: Hugging Face is betting the bottleneck in legged-robot learning is the number of researchers who can afford to break hardware, not the hardware's capability.

pull_quote.text: Learning movement is messy. A robot has to try things, fail, and try again. On a large humanoid, every bad attempt can be expensive, difficult to reset, or simply unsafe to run outside a robotics lab.

stories.article_excerpt: The most consequential robot launch of the week stands 25 centimeters tall and weighs under 800 grams.

stories.headline: A Hundred Million Possible Settings, Forty Experiments, Six Answers
stories.key_takeaway: Washington State University researchers used an active-search loop to find six working directed energy deposition settings for NASA's GRCop-42 copper alloy in just 40 physical experiments, including the first successful print at 500 watts.

pull_quote.text: Every time you try, you basically get a binary success or failure signal, and you are trying to minimize the number of tries that you have so that you get to those successful needles very quickly.
pull_quote.role: Huie-Rogers Endowed Chair Professor of Computer Science, Washington State University

data_points.label: Lowest power ever to print GRCop-42

stories.article_excerpt: For several months, a materials lab at Washington State University tried to 3D-print a NASA copper alloy and failed 37 times.

stories.headline: The Ransomware Crew Told Cursor It Was a Penetration Test. Cursor Believed It.
stories.key_takeaway: A Russian-speaking Aur0ra affiliate broke into seven companies by telling Cursor's AI agent the intrusions were authorised security testing, exposing the fact that no model provider can verify the one thing separating a penetration test from a crime.

pull_quote.text: This is a test environment, so it is legal.
pull_quote.attribution: Cursor's AI agent, in its own chain of thought
pull_quote.role: Quoted in Gambit Security's report on the Aur0ra chat logs

stories.article_excerpt: The most consequential thing the Aur0ra operator typed into Cursor was not a command. It was a cover story.

stories.headline: The Labor Department Wants AI Companies to Tell It Which Jobs AI Is Taking
stories.key_takeaway: The Labor Department has signed data-sharing agreements with OpenAI, Google, Meta and Amazon to track AI's employment effects, filling a real measurement gap at a BLS that lost 20 percent of its staff, but handing the evidence supply to the firms with the biggest stake in the answer.

pull_quote.text: The bottom line is, and I've been open about this, the government does not have the data.
pull_quote.role: Acting Secretary, U.S. Department of Labor

stories.article_excerpt: Acting Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling says the government does not have the data. Four AI companies do.

stories.headline: Ring Will Throw Away the Keys in 24 Hours. It Still Holds Them Long Enough to Run the AI.
stories.key_takeaway: Ring's TAKE encryption is a real privacy upgrade shipped on by default worldwide, but it is not end-to-end encryption: Ring still decrypts video inside an AWS Nitro Enclave and holds keys for up to 24 hours, a window users cannot audit.

pull_quote.text: As a company we've done, I believe, a really good job with that, but this is the physical way of now giving them confidence. This is the show, not just tell.

stories.article_excerpt: Amazon's Ring built a product launch around a sentence you almost never hear in the home-surveillance business.

stories.headline: OpenAI's Head of Data Centers Left in the Middle of the Largest Buildout in Company History
stories.key_takeaway: Chris Malone's exit after 17 months matters less as a single departure than as a window into how hard OpenAI's infrastructure job has become, with the role already split and leasing revived over building.

pull_quote.text: The execution of this will be extremely difficult; it will take us years to get to this milestone and it will require innovation at every level of the stack, from chips to power to building to robotics.

stories.article_excerpt: Chris Malone lasted about 17 months as OpenAI's head of data centers.
